name: hacksaw
desc: The saw with a fine tight blade made for cutting through metal.
prose: A hacksaw is the saw you reach for when the job is metal, not wood - a thin, fine-toothed blade stretched tight in a sturdy bow of a frame. Where a big wood saw would just skid and screech, the hacksaw bites slowly through a pipe or a bolt or a padlock, back and forth, back and forth, leaving a little pile of bright metal dust. Change the blade when it goes blunt. Patient and tough, it cuts the things nothing else will.

lines: Rough scratchy paper, gritty and tough,
rub it on wood to make it smooth;
it wears the bumps and splinters off -
A rubber cup upon a stick,
push it down on the blocked-up drain;
squelch and pull with all your might -
A long-handled tool with a flat blade end,
chop the weeds and break the soil;
drag it through the vegetable patch -
a gardener's friend for the digging toil.
A long iron bar with a curved flat end,
shove it under and lever it up;
prise the lid off the heavy crate -
pop! with a heave and a tug.
